notes.migration_version_drift: apply_migration stamps its own timestamp, so production versions do not match repo filename prefixes. MEASURED: 21 of 48 applied rows carry an MCP stamp; 27 carry a repo-shaped stamp. The NAMES match the repo files exactly in every case, so which migration ran is never ambiguous. Two consequences to know. (1) `supabase db diff`/`db push` sees version skew and would consider those repo files unapplied. (2) The MCP stamps also reorder this slice relative to the repo: production ran merchant_customers, business_categories, delivery_presets, workspace_activation, preset_commands, whereas the repo filenames order workspace_activation second. Checked and harmless — workspace_activation depends only on business_accounts, couranr_delivery_requests, couranr_merchant_workspaces, couranr_require_active_member and profiles, none of which come from the categories or presets migrations, and neither of those depends on activation. Both orderings are valid. Not corrected by hand: rewriting supabase_migrations.schema_migrations is an owner-gated production-ledger repair and is riskier than the drift it would fix. If a re-push ever does replay these, couranr_workspace_activation opens with a guard that RAISES when the table already exists, so it fails loudly rather than corrupting silently.

notes.container_restart_hazards: A container restart in this session produced THREE misleading conditions in a row, all of which look like code problems and are not. Check these before diagnosing anything after a restart. (1) THE WORKING TREE MOVES. It came back on claude/couranr-phase-0-readiness-se3gdz at 0042cbe - a different branch at an old commit - so the migration files did not exist and the fix commit was not a valid git object. Recovery is `git fetch origin <branch> && git checkout -B <branch> origin/<branch>`; the work is safe ONLY because it was pushed after every commit. (2) THE CLONE IS SHALLOW. tests/couranr-implementation-ledger.test.ts FAILS on a shallow clone by design rather than skipping, so this shows up as a red test that is actually the guard working. Fix with `git fetch --unshallow` (250 commits -> 1152 here). (3) node_modules IS STALE, and this one is the dangerous one because it FAILS GREEN. After the restart node_modules belonged to the other branch, which predates B01's move to @supabase/ssr. Two test FILES failed to resolve their imports and never loaded, so 84 tests silently did not run - and vitest still printed `1548 passed`, which reads as success. Only comparing the count against the known 1632 caught it. Fix with `npm ci`. ALWAYS check `Test Files X passed (Y)` for X = Y, not just the passing count.

notes.b05_wiring_decision: DECISION, and it OVERTURNS the plan recorded in b05_wiring_deferred_deliberately: wire the substrate at NEITHER site. A 7-agent design workflow (three opposing priors, each attacked on live-money grounds) converged on this, and I verified its load-bearing claims myself rather than taking them. (1) couranr_create_payment_obligation - CHANGE NOTHING. The duplicate a key would prevent is already impossible by a STRONGER mechanism, verified live: couranr_po_one_live_per_request is UNIQUE (request_id) WHERE payment_state <> 'cancelled'. That is structural and keyed on request_id, which the substrate's scope (purpose, actor_type, actor_id, key) does not even contain - so the substrate is strictly NARROWER here, not redundant. Worse, wiring it would BREAK a decided behaviour: the sole caller passes a constant key, so a PAY-002 requote (cancel old, create new, new amount) presents the same key with a different request hash and gets `mismatch` - permanently, since mismatch clears only on expiry. The merchant could never re-pay a re-quoted delivery. (2) couranr_begin_payment_capture - do not wire the substrate either. It cannot dedupe here by construction: actor_id is IN the unique index, so two operators on the shared queue both get `proceed` - and a second operator is the exact threat the code's own comment names. (3) BUILD INSTEAD a discriminating command. The live function's early return is non-erroring, so the caller cannot distinguish 'I moved it' from 'it was already there'. Correctness therefore rests entirely on a TypeScript pre-check at lib/couranr/fulfillment/commands.ts:284-296 that is NOT atomic with the SQL call, so a concurrent caller can slip between them. Proposal: a NEW function public.couranr_begin_payment_capture_attempt(uuid, uuid) returning (outcome, obligation) with outcome in (begun, already_in_flight, already_captured); only `begun` may reach Stripe. New NAME, not an overload, so PostgREST resolution is not in play. The live 2-arg function stays untouched and the TS pre-check STAYS - the new command makes SQL agree with it so a future route that forgets the pre-check fails closed.
notes.b05_substrate_reachability: MEASURED, and it constrains how the substrate can ever be used: has_schema_privilege('authenticator', 'private','USAGE') = false, while service_role has it. Combined with supabase-js routing .rpc() at the client's configured schema (default `public`, and lib/supabaseAdmin.ts sets no db.schema), the substrate in `private` is NOT callable from the TypeScript layer as things stand. It is reachable only from INSIDE a public SQL function running as service_role. That is consistent with the intended design - wire it into SQL commands, not into routes - but it means any future plan to call it from a route needs either a public wrapper or a db.schema change, and should say which.
notes.b05_capture_stripe_window: MEASURED: all 12 capture_pending obligations are 69-138 hours old. Every one is past Stripe's 24-hour idempotency-key cache, so captureIdempotencyKey(ob.id, ob.version) no longer dedupes any of them at the provider. Stripe is NOT the backstop for these rows; the TypeScript pre-check is.
